The flag of Israel is a horizontal rectangular flag with two indigo (dark blue or dark navy) stripes at the top and bottom, each occupying one-ninth of the flag's height, and a white stripe in the middle that occupies the remaining seven-ninths. In the center of the white stripe is a blue Star of David (Magen David), a six-pointed star that is a symbol of Judaism and, by extension, the Jewish people.

The colors of the flag are white and blue, with the indigo used for the stripes and the Star of David. The blue used on the flag is traditionally called "techelet," a color associated with the sky and the sea in Jewish tradition. The white and blue colors are also reminiscent of the tallit, or prayer shawl, which is traditionally white with blue stripes.

The design of the flag was created by artist and poet David Wolffsohn, who was inspired by a vision of the Star of David on a tallit. The flag was officially adopted on October 28, 1948, shortly after the establishment of the State of Israel.
